Holcim Liban SAL Files for Insolvency, Disrupting Lebanon’s Construction Sector

BEIRUT, June 6 — Holcim Liban SAL, one of Lebanon’s largest producers of construction materials, has entered insolvency proceedings, the company confirmed Thursday, sending shockwaves through the country’s already beleaguered construction sector.

The move places Holcim Liban SAL’s operations in jeopardy, with immediate effects on cement production and delivery. “We regret to announce that, due to severe financial constraints, Holcim Liban SAL has filed for insolvency,” the company said in a statement. “Production lines have been halted and shipments to clients are suspended until further notice.”

Industry analysts say the collapse could further undermine Lebanon’s post-crisis reconstruction efforts. “Holcim Liban was a pillar of local supply,” said Hadi Matar, a construction sector analyst based in Beirut. “The insolvency is likely to lead to critical shortages and price volatility, given the limited number of domestic producers.”

The company, which employs more than 300 workers at its Chekka plant, has not detailed the full impact on its workforce. Employees reported being told not to report to work and expressed fears over unpaid wages. “We don’t know if we’ll be paid this month,” said Marwan Khoury, a plant employee for over a decade. “People have families and loans. This is devastating.”

Lebanon’s construction industry has faced mounting difficulties amid the country’s prolonged economic crisis, with soaring costs for imported raw materials and energy. The Lebanese Union of Construction Workers urged authorities to intervene. “We call on the government to protect the rights of workers and ensure that the sector survives this blow,” the union said in a statement.

The insolvency proceedings remain ongoing. Holcim Liban SAL said it is working with court-appointed administrators to assess restructuring options, but warned that “operations cannot resume until a viable plan is agreed.”
